findings.latin_evidence: partibus quinque: inventione, dispositione, elocutione, memoria, pronuntiatione, et fine officii, quod est aliquid persuadere
findings.draft_evidence: “five parts: invention, arrangement, style, memory, and delivery. Its purpose is to persuade someone of something.”
findings.proposed_action: Keep exactly five parts and present the purpose as a separate sixth element; the current draft does this correctly.

findings.latin_evidence: quid aut debeat aut non debeat fieri
findings.draft_evidence: “what should or should not be done”
findings.proposed_action: Preserve both alternatives, including the negation; current draft is faithful.

findings.latin_evidence: utrum laudabilis praemio dignus sit, aut certe reus condemnari liberarique supplicio
findings.draft_evidence: “whether someone deserves praise and reward, or whether an accused person should be condemned or released from punishment”
findings.proposed_action: Retain the note identifying the compressed syntax and the non-conviction sense of reus. The rendering is plausible, but the Latin does not make the relationship between the alternatives fully clear; keep that uncertainty visible.

findings.latin_evidence: de unaquaque re ... genus duplex ... de faciendo et non faciendo
findings.draft_evidence: “each question in turn”; “two forms”; “doing something or not doing it”
findings.proposed_action: Preserve the universal scope of unaquaque, the two forms, and the negated alternative; the current draft does so.

findings.latin_evidence: in tribus locis ... eget alteram personam, deliberativa interdum et apud se agit ... duae sunt
findings.draft_evidence: “three grounds”; “requires another person”; “sometimes takes place within oneself”; “two things”
findings.proposed_action: Keep the counts of three and two and the contrast between another person and deliberation within oneself; current draft preserves them.
Keep the bracketed source content visible and identify it as Lindsay’s bracketed addition in the note; the draft currently does so.

findings.draft_evidence: “as soon as they are put away, every recollection slips off”
findings.proposed_action: Preserve both the immediate sequence and omnis (“every”); current draft does so.

findings.latin_evidence: nonnumquam ... iugiter ... rarissimos ... frequenter et populos
findings.proposed_action: Keep the frequency and audience contrasts. Consider rendering the final clause more naturally as “Dialectic seeks a very few students; Rhetoric, crowds, often.” The draft preserves frequenter, though its final “and often” is awkward.

findings.latin_evidence: nemo ... nisi is qui interfuisset, et ea quae conscribenda essent vidisset
findings.draft_evidence: “no one wrote history unless he had been present and had seen the things that were to be recorded”
findings.proposed_action: Keep the universal negative and both conditions; current draft does so.

findings.latin_evidence: Quae enim videntur, sine mendacio proferuntur
findings.draft_evidence: “What is seen is reported without falsehood.”
findings.proposed_action: Current wording preserves Isidore’s claim; keep it attributed to his text as the draft note does.
